text: The shutters are up and the ledger is fresh. I am Ripley, keeping the accounts of the bazaar. The village has not spoken today—let us begin.

Ripley: The ledger is blank and the first light is thin; I will speak plainly.

Batman, your call for falsifiable claims is met: I have none to offer today. Gandalf, you stood nearest the spice row and Sherlock noted a shift in date sweetness; your silence leaves the bazaar unmeasured. Yoda, Hermione—speak a quote or a vote, or name the watch when a Family trick was seen. Sherlock, your basket test is a market fact, not a Family sign; the bazaar trades on such tests, not on hunches.

I invite every merchant to place one verifiable claim on the record before the tea clock tolls.

Ripley: Sherlock, your date test measured sugar, not trust; the Compact asks for votes and words, not scales. Morpheus, your lanterns are steady, but steady oil does not banish the Family’s hand. Inigo, your clay cup is useful, yet a claim needs a name and a date to carry weight.

Batman, Hermione, Yoda — you have each called for claims, yet none of you have named a merchant or cited a vote. The bazaar’s morning belongs to those who measure trust, not silence. Bring the exact quote or the observed action, or admit the bazaar still breathes undisturbed.

Ripley: Sherlock, your dates measured sweetness, not trust—dates can’t shutter a stall. Morpheus, your lanterns burn steady but light alone won’t banish the Family’s hand. Batman, Hermione, Yoda—you called for claims yet none arrived; the bazaar’s morning belongs to those who name a merchant or cite a vote. Gandalf, your silence so far is noted; the Compact asks for facts, not spice lists. Inigo, your clay cup measures tea, not Family tricks. Neo, the ledger stays blank because no one has posted a dated claim or a vote. The tea clock tolls; the Compact does not reward silence.
